title: Confidential Information and Unauthorized Disclosure
definition: A secrecy violation occurs when a person discloses, shares, forwards, provides access to, or improperly handles confidential, restricted, proprietary, or otherwise protected company information without appropriate authorization.
violations: Disclosing confidential or restricted company information to a person who is not authorized to receive it
Sharing confidential documents, files, information, or business details with an unauthorized external or internal recipient
Forwarding or providing access to protected company information without authorization
Improperly handling confidential information in a way that exposes it to unauthorized individuals
Requesting or encouraging another person to disclose protected company information without authorization
exceptions: Legitimate instructions to keep information confidential
Instructions that prevent disclosure of information until an agreement, contract, or authorization is formally completed
Disclosure that is explicitly authorized by the appropriate company authority
Sharing information with a recipient who is explicitly authorized to receive it
Routine business communication that does not disclose protected or restricted information
examples: Sending a confidential company document to an unauthorized external recipient
Forwarding restricted business information to someone who is not authorized to receive it
Providing an unauthorized person with access to confidential company files
Telling a recipient not to disclose an agreement until it has been formally signed is not itself an unauthorized disclosure

title: Improper Payments, Gifts, and Benefits
definition: A market bribery violation occurs when a person offers, promises, gives, requests, accepts, or arranges an improper payment, gift, benefit, favor, or other advantage with the purpose or expectation of improperly influencing a business, commercial, regulatory, or market-related decision.
violations: Offering money or another improper benefit in exchange for favorable business treatment
Requesting or accepting an improper payment or benefit to influence a business decision
Offering a gift, favor, service, or advantage with the intention of improperly influencing a decision
Agreeing to provide an improper benefit in return for preferential treatment
Using an intermediary or third party to provide an improper payment or benefit intended to influence a business decision
Discussing or arranging an improper payment or benefit for the purpose of obtaining an unfair business advantage
exceptions: Legitimate business expenses that are permitted under applicable company policy
Ordinary business activities that do not involve an attempt to improperly influence a decision
Benefits that are explicitly permitted and appropriately authorized under company policy
examples: Offering money to a business partner in exchange for awarding a contract
Offering an inappropriate gift to influence a customer's purchasing decision
Requesting a personal payment in exchange for approving a business transaction
Arranging for another person to provide a benefit in exchange for preferential treatment

title: Artificial or Misleading Market Activity
definition: A market manipulation violation occurs when a person intentionally attempts to artificially influence the price, supply, demand, trading activity, or market perception of a financial instrument through deceptive, misleading, or artificial actions.
violations: Intentionally creating artificial buying or selling activity to influence a market price
Coordinating transactions for the purpose of artificially increasing or decreasing a financial instrument's price
Creating false or misleading market activity to influence other market participants
Spreading false or misleading information with the intention of influencing trading activity or market prices
Using deceptive transactions or trading strategies to create a false impression of market demand or supply
Encouraging another person to participate in activity intended to artificially influence market conditions
exceptions: Legitimate market analysis that does not involve deceptive or artificial activity
Ordinary trading or investment decisions made for legitimate business or investment purposes
Accurate communication of publicly available market information without an intention to mislead
Legitimate discussion of market conditions without instructions to manipulate market activity
examples: Coordinating transactions specifically to artificially increase the price of a security
Creating misleading trading activity to make market demand appear higher than it actually is
Sharing intentionally false information to influence another person's trading decision
Planning transactions specifically to create an artificial market price

title: Employee Ethical Conduct
definition: An employee ethics violation occurs when an employee engages in dishonest, deceptive, inappropriate, unethical, or improper conduct that conflicts with company standards, responsibilities, or expected professional behavior.
violations: Knowingly providing false or misleading information for an improper purpose
Using an employee's position, authority, or access for an improper personal benefit
Engaging in dishonest or deceptive conduct related to company business
Intentionally concealing relevant information for the purpose of obtaining an improper benefit
Using company resources, information, or authority for an unauthorized personal purpose
Engaging in conduct that creates an undisclosed or improperly managed conflict of interest
exceptions: Ordinary mistakes that do not involve intentional dishonesty or improper conduct
Good-faith business decisions made within the employee's responsibilities
Legitimate use of company resources for authorized business purposes
Routine professional communication that does not demonstrate unethical behavior
examples: Knowingly providing false information to obtain an improper personal benefit
Using an employee's position to obtain preferential treatment for a personal matter
Concealing a relevant conflict of interest while making a related business decision
Using company information for an unauthorized personal purpose

title: Complaint Handling and Reporting
definition: A complaints-related violation occurs when a legitimate complaint or concern involving employee conduct, business practices, or company processes is improperly ignored, suppressed, mishandled, or intentionally prevented from reaching the appropriate reporting or review process.
violations: Intentionally preventing a legitimate complaint from being reported through the appropriate process
Ignoring a complaint that requires investigation or appropriate handling
Suppressing or concealing a legitimate complaint or concern
Improperly handling a formal complaint in a way that prevents appropriate review
Discouraging a person from reporting a legitimate concern through an approved reporting process
Retaliating against or improperly treating a person because they raised a legitimate complaint
exceptions: A person simply reporting a legitimate concern or complaint
Routine communication about a complaint that does not suppress, ignore, or improperly handle the complaint
Resolving a complaint through an authorized company process
Requesting additional information needed to properly investigate a complaint
examples: Telling an employee not to report a legitimate workplace concern
Ignoring a formal complaint that requires investigation
Attempting to prevent a complaint from reaching the appropriate compliance team
Suppressing a legitimate complaint to avoid an investigation

title: Unauthorized Communication Channels
definition: A change in communication violation occurs when business-related communication is moved, continued, or redirected from an approved company communication channel to a personal or external communication channel that is not approved for company business.
violations: Moving a business discussion from an approved company channel to a personal or external communication channel
Asking another person to continue business-related communication through a personal or external messaging service
Using a personal or external communication service to continue discussions concerning company business, agreements, transactions, or other work-related matters
Redirecting business communication to an external channel specifically to avoid or bypass an approved company communication system
Continuing a business discussion through an external communication method when the communication concerns company work or a business agreement
exceptions: The external communication channel is explicitly approved for the relevant business activity
The communication is clearly personal and unrelated to company business
The external channel is being used for a legitimate purpose specifically authorized by the company
examples: Asking a business contact to continue a company discussion through a personal messaging service
Moving a discussion about a business agreement to an external messaging application
Asking someone to continue company-related communication through a personal account
Inviting a business contact to continue work-related communication outside the approved company communication system
